_readme: Recall candidates not in the base (scratch/recall-fts-*.json adds and targets, recall-probe.json adds, judge-named sale-consideration targets), deduped by loose name. Each lands at the one rebuild as a ledger recall addition and is judged for membership in the delta grind. Dropped: R3 joint vehicles (Finacity, WeServeHomes, ServiceMaster JV) and R1 bios with nothing more (FirstLook, Vanguard Solar).

rows.name: Asera
rows.basis: the firm's company whose assets SEEC bought (judge j12)

rows.name: Asia Innovations Group
rows.basis: Company Shareholder Voting Agreement for "Asia Innovations Group Limited ... (the 'Company')" signed by "KPCB CHINA FUND II, L.P." as a company shareholder (the merger was later terminated). KPCB China fund position: IN under X1's provisional reading.

rows.name: Atlantic Money
rows.basis: Growth Business, 2022-07-22: Atlantic Money's extension "is in addition to $4.5m (£3.8m) in initial seed funding from investors including Index Ventures and Ribbit & Kleiner Perkins"; Wikipedia Atlantic_Money names Kleiner Perkins in the $7.5M 2022 seed. Entry Seed 2022; acquired by Deel (FinTech Futures, 2025-03-26).

rows.name: Broadband Office
rows.basis: 10-K bio: 'Broadband Office, an internet start-up funded by Kleiner-Perkins Caulfield & Byer, Microsoft and Sun' (2000-01). Not in base.

rows.name: Cimlinc
rows.basis: "Cimlinc raised $26 million in funding from venture capital firms such as Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers. John Doerr ... was on the company's board of directors for 10 years. Cimlinc was sold to Boeing." CAD/CAM maker, named Cadlinc until Nov 1985 (history-of-cad: KPCB among investors in four rounds). Not in the base; pre-2006, round undatable from this record.

rows.name: CryoCor
rows.basis: S-1 2005 Ex.4.2, the Series D (June 2003) Amended and Restated Investors' Rights Agreement, is signed by 'KLEINER PERKINS CAUFIELD & BYERS VIII', 'KPCB LIFE SCIENCES ZAIBATSU FUND II' and 'KPCB VIII FOUNDERS FUND' as investors (not a 5% holder at IPO).

rows.name: Cryogen
rows.basis: AMS/Cryogen merger agreement closing condition: 'Termination of Management Rights Agreement. The letter agreement regarding "Management Rights", dated as of January 27, 1997, between the Company and Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VIII'.

rows.name: CVie Therapeutics
rows.basis: 13D by Ivy Blue Holdings and 'KPCB China Fund II, L.P. ... the 100% owner of Ivy Blue Holdings' for shares issued to former CVie Investments shareholders in the merger; 8-K: James Huang 'a former Director of CVie and Managing Partner, KPCB China'.

rows.name: Daisie
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2019-05-20: Daisie "closed on $2.5 million in seed funding ... The round was led by Founders Fund, which contributed $1.5 million. Other investors included 8VC, Kleiner Perkins, and newer VC firm Shrug Capital". Seed 2019 (London).

rows.name: Dbank
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2022-07-27: Islamabad-based Dbank "has raised $17.6 million in a seed round, the largest in Pakistan, co-led by Sequoia Capital Southeast Asia ... and Kleiner Perkins", with Nubank participating. Seed 2022 (Pakistan).

rows.name: Drop
rows.basis: Wikipedia Drop (company): "In September 2014, Drop raised $6.5 million in a Series A round led by Mayfield Fund with additional investment from previous backers Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, First Round Capital, and Cowboy Ventures." KP was a pre-Series-A (seed) backer; entry year before 2014 not stated. Google News found no second source: medium confidence. Dublin-based.

rows.name: EEStor
rows.basis: Wikipedia EEStor: "In July 2005, Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers invested $3 million in EEStor" and on 2013-12-30 ZENN bought "Series A preferred shares of EEStor (includes Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers shares ...)"; Wikipedia ZENN Motor Company: "KPCB invested $3 million in EEStor in 2005 for approximately 20% ownership". Series A 2005 (single-source family: Wikipedia plus ZENN's 2013 disclosure it quotes).

rows.name: Evant
rows.basis: Merger agreement 'by and among Manhattan Associates, Inc., Madison Acquisition Corp., Evant, Inc., and Ted Schlein, as Shareholder Representative ... c/o Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers'; no fund named in the filing, Dealroom has KP in Evant's June 2004 $15M Series C.

rows.name: Evervault
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2019-10-16: "Evervault raises $3.2M from Sequoia, Kleiner for an API to build apps with privacy baked in"; TechCrunch 2021-08-18: Dublin-based Evervault "is backed by ... Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins and Index Ventures". Seed 2019 (Dublin, IE); the $16M Series A (FinSMEs 2020-05-22) followed.

rows.name: FreeMarkets
rows.basis: 2001 proxy: Doerr's holdings include '283,323 shares held by KPCB Holdings, Inc. as nominee for the account of KPCB IX-A; and ... 8,759 shares ... KPCB IX-B'; Doerr a director 'since October 1999', i.e. before the December 1999 IPO. Press (TheStreet) dates KP's late-stage pre-IPO round to late 1999 (Growth under D4). Cenveo's 2009 fairness table also names KP as a FreeMarkets seller to Ariba (2004).

rows.name: Geocast Network Systems
rows.basis: S-4/A 2021 bio: 'Geocast Network Systems, a broadband infrastructure company backed by Mayfield, Kleiner Perkins and Institutional Venture Partners'.

rows.name: GO Corporation
rows.basis: Bio: 'two Bay Area, Kleiner Perkins startups (GO Corp. and Excite)'. GO Corporation (pen computing, 1987-94, John Doerr on the board) is not in the base; its spin-out Eo Computer is.

rows.name: Greenlight.com
rows.basis: CarsDirect Fifth A&R Investor Rights Agreement (2001-02-06): 'Agreement of Merger ... among the Company, CD Merger Sub, Inc., Greenlight.com, Inc. KPCB Holdings, Inc., Asbury-Everest Holdings L.L.C.' (KPCB Holdings as a Greenlight.com securityholder party).

rows.name: Himax Display
rows.basis: 6-K 2013-07-22: 'Google will join the core group of HDI shareholders including KPCB Holdings, Inc., Khosla Ventures I, L.P. and Intel Capital'; Himax Technologies holds 81.5% of HDI (private subsidiary, minority venture stake).

rows.name: HomeGrocer
rows.basis: 424B4 2001: 'Lead investors in the private round of financings include Amazon.com, Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, Hummer Winblad Venture Partners' (HomeGrocer.com).

rows.name: Hybritech
rows.basis: Wikipedia Ivor Royston: "Financier Brook Byers, of Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers ... His firm provided the $300,000 start-up funding" for Hybritech (founded 1978; IPO 1981; bought by Eli Lilly 1986 for $480M). Pre-EDGAR; single source family: medium confidence. The Hybritech article itself now redirects to Beckman Coulter.

rows.name: Icarian
rows.basis: Registration-rights signature blocks for Icarian's former holders: 'KPCB Java Fund ... Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VIII ... KPCB VIII Founders Fund'; the 8-K press release names Kleiner Perkins among Icarian investors joining Workstream's shareholders.

rows.name: Imagic
rows.basis: Wikipedia Imagic: "Grubb and Dougherty pitched venture capitalist Kleiner Perkins and Merrill Pickard, ultimately raising $2 million in seed capital". Pre-EDGAR, single source: medium confidence.

rows.name: InnerCool Therapies
rows.basis: the firm's position behind the Cardium row (judge j06, medium)

rows.name: iScribe
rows.basis: 'iScribe is backed by six leading venture capital firms in healthcare and e-commerce technology, Kleiner Perkins Caufield and Byers, Mayfield Fund, Skyline Ventures, Galen Partners, Domain Associates and Gleacher Capital Partners.'

rows.name: Jetti Resources
rows.basis: BetaKit, 2019-07-17: Jetti "has raised more than $24 million CAD to date ... all of which was from a Series A raised by US investors, in 2017. Disclosed investors in the startup include DNS Capital, Kleiner Perkins, and Zoma Capital." Series A 2017 (Vancouver copper-leaching technology).

rows.name: Keplar
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2025-09-17: "the two-year-old company announced that it raised $3.4 million in seed funding led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from SV Angel, Common Metal, and South Park Commons." Seed 2025; not yet on the firm's live list.

rows.name: Kibu.com
rows.basis: Wikipedia Kibu.com: "In February 2000, Kibu.com received an investment of US$22 million from ... Jim Clark, ... Tom Jermoluk, the venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, and CNET chairman Shelby Bonnie". Google News has no 2000 coverage; single source: medium confidence.

rows.name: LendUp
rows.basis: Los Angeles Times, 2016-09-27: "LendUp is backed by ... venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, as well as GV"; Wikipedia LendUp lists KPCB among its equity investors. Entry year not stated (first_seen is the evidence year); shut down 2021 after the CFPB order.

rows.name: LMArena
rows.basis: Pulse 2.0, 2025-05-26: "$100 million in seed funding led by a16z and UC Investments ... with participation from Lightspeed, Laude Ventures, Felicis, Kleiner Perkins and The House Fund"; SiliconANGLE 2026-01-06 (https://siliconangle.com/2026/01/06/ai-evaluation-startup-lmarena-raises-150m-1-7b-valuation/): the $150M Series A "also drew contributions from ... Kleiner Perkins". Entry Seed, 2025. Wikipedia Arena.ai carries the same two rounds.

rows.name: Medibuy
rows.basis: 8-K 2016: 'Medibuy received over $100 million in venture funding from Kleiner-Perkins, Sequoia, Oak Investments'; Reticulate Micro's 1-K (2025) repeats 'backed by Venture Capitalists such as Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Oak'.

rows.name: MiniStor Peripherals
rows.basis: Wikipedia MiniStor: "MiniStor received seed funding from multiple investors, including Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, amounting to $4.2 million by the time of its incorporation" (founded May 1991). Pre-EDGAR; EDGAR (CIK 922871) holds only the 2011 revocation, so Wikipedia is the only source read: medium confidence.

rows.name: Nanoleaf
rows.basis: University of Toronto News, 2014-03-28: Nanoleaf "has banked support from ... Li Ka Shing ... and Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm, Kleiner Perkins"; founder: "We ended up getting funding from them [Horizons Ventures], as well as a Silicon Valley venture capital group called Kleiner Perkins." First institutional round 2014 (entry round unnamed).

rows.name: NexGen
rows.basis: AMD Schedule 13D on NexGen, 1995-12-19: "The stockholders of NexGen which have executed Voting Agreements are Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers IV, Olivetti Holdings, ... Compaq" with KPCB IV holding 1,360,869 shares. Wikipedia: KP joined "in a later round" after Compaq and Olivetti (pre-1995 IPO private entry; the year of entry is not in the filing). Acquired by AMD 1996.

rows.name: NFTfi
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2021-11-16: NFTfi "has raised a seed round of $5 million ... Early-stage crypto fund 1kx led the round, with Ashton Kutcher's Sound Ventures, Maven 11, Scalar Capital, Kleiner Perkins and others participating". Seed 2021 (South Africa).

rows.name: Oblix
rows.basis: 'Oblix, a technology firm that has been acquired by Oracle and was a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and APAX Partners' (he worked there 2000-03).

rows.name: Oura
rows.basis: Registration Rights Agreement of March 31, 2026 (pre-IPO) signed under 'INVESTORS: KPCB Holdings, Inc. By: /s/ Susan Biglieri ... Chief Financial Officer'; the entry round is not given in this record.

rows.name: Picaboo
rows.basis: Wikipedia Picaboo (photo-book maker, Palo Alto, founded 2002): "Series-A funding was secured from Kleiner Perkins and Softbank." Year of the Series A not given (first photo editor launched 2005); Google News finds only the unrelated Picaboo that became Snapchat. Single source: medium confidence.

rows.name: Plexus Computers
rows.basis: Wikipedia Plexus Computers: after 1980 the founders "secured over $18.5 million in startup capital from 17 large investment firms—including Kleiner Perkins, Hambrecht & Quist, and L.F. Rothschild". Pre-EDGAR, single source: medium confidence; entry year approximate (1981).

rows.name: Portera
rows.basis: 'Mr. Rhoades was responsible for mergers and acquisitions and strategic partnerships for Portera, a Kleiner-Perkins company from March 2000 to June 2002.'

rows.name: Q Entertainment
rows.basis: The firm's own site lists it, parsed from its own captures but never built into base: kpcb.com/china/english/portfolio/ (2010: "Q Entertainment ... A third party game design studio in Japan", Tokyo), kpcb.com/companies/q-entertainment 2012-2018 (teams China and Digital, status Private) and the kleinerperkins.com/partnerships logo grid 2021-2024. A site listing suffices (§1); KPCB China team, so X1 applies (flag kpcb_china). The only archive-parsed company missing from base: every other unmatched parsed slug resolves to a base row under a name variant. Its archive years (2010, 2012-2018, 2021-2024) were folded into base row q (Q.ai, the 2023 deal Apple bought), which is why it looks absent: split it back out as its own row.

rows.name: ReplayTV
rows.basis: ReplayTV's 2000 S-1 (withdrawn IPO): 'Entities affiliated with KPCB Holdings (William R. Hearst III) ... 7,870,968' Series D and '133,333' Series E preferred, 'All shares are held by KPCB Holdings Inc., as nominee'; SONICblue's merger names Hearst III, c/o KPCB, as Stockholder Agent.

rows.name: Series
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2023-09-26: Series is "Backed by $25 million in funding across seed and Series A rounds led by 776 and Basis Set Ventures, with participation from Pear VC, Kleiner Perkins, Day One Ventures ...". Co-founder Brexton Pham previously worked at KP (named separately); KP is named as a participating investor. Seed/Series A 2023, round of entry not separated.

rows.name: Sigma Systems
rows.basis: Share Purchase Agreement dated 2002-07-24 among Liberate, its Ontario sub, Sigma Systems Group (Canada) Inc. and 'the holders listed on the signature pages', signed 'KLEINER PERKINS CAUFIELD & BYERS By: /s/Raymond Lane, Partner' alongside Redwood Ventures IV and Morgan Stanley.

rows.name: Skew
rows.basis: UK Tech Investment News, 2019-09-25: crypto derivatives analytics start-up Skew "has raised $2 million in seed funding from several venture capital firms, including Silicon Valley icon Kleiner Perkins", round led by firstminute capital. Seed 2019 (London; later bought by Coinbase).

rows.name: Spectrum HoloByte
rows.basis: Spectrum HoloByte / MicroProse Inc. proxy, 1996-07-29: Vinod Khosla "has been a director ... of Spectrum HoloByte since its inception in September 1992" and his line "includes 648,172 shares of Common Stock held by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VI; 80,197 shares ... held by KPCB VI Founders Fund". Wikipedia: "In 1992, Spectrum HoloByte received an investment from Kleiner Perkins". Not the Sid Meier MicroProse it bought in 1993.

rows.name: Terradot
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2026-02-06: "Terradot's investor list includes Gigascale Capital, Google, Kleiner Perkins, and Microsoft." The rp-2024 query ("Kleiner Perkins" led 2024) surfaced LatamList 2024-12-17 "Terradot raises $58M series A round" (not read), so entry is taken as the 2024 Series A: confirm the round before stage. Carbon removal, California/Brazil.

rows.name: Total Entertainment Network
rows.basis: Wikipedia Total Entertainment Network: the firm's "archived Kleiner Perkins consumer-media portfolio page lists Total Entertainment Network" (kpcb.com/keiretsu/ConsumerMedia.html, 1999 capture), and its first venture round came from "Vinod Khosla, a general partner at Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers"; Wikipedia Pogo.com: TEN/Pogo was created "in conjunction with investment from Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers led by partner Vinod Khosla". A firm site listing (§1). The capture itself was NOT fetched: the Internet Archive is in the machine-wide cooldown; read it at the pre-2008 archive fill.

rows.name: Vividence
rows.basis: Keynote/Vividence Agreement and Plan of Reorganization (2004-09-10): lease matters 'subject to the approval of the Shareholders' Representative upon consultation with Partech International, Inc. and Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (KPCB)'. KP is consulted as a Vividence holder; no share count given.

rows.name: Yapp
rows.basis: Observer (Betabeat), 2012-04-06: Yapp "announced a round of funding from Kleiner Perkins, North Bridge Venture Partners, Cue Ball, and other individual investors"; Business Insider 2012-04-04 (https://www.businessinsider.com/what-is-yapp-2012-4) same. Seed 2012.

rows.name: Zambeel
rows.basis: Komag S-1 bio: 'startup companies such as Zambeel Inc., a Kleiner/ Perkins and NEA storage startup'.
